title: The cokernel of the naive cotangent complex is the module of Kähler differentials
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and let $\mathrm{NL}_{S/R}=\bigl(I/I^2\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }\bigoplus_{s\in S}S\,\mathrm d[s]\bigr)$ be its naive cotangent complex, formed with the canonical presentation $\gamma:R[S]\to S$, $I=\ker\gamma$, as in [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]. Then the $S$-linear map $\pi:\bigoplus_{s\in S}S\,\mathrm d[s]\to\Omega_{S/R}$, $\mathrm d[s]\mapsto\mathrm ds$ ($\Omega_{S/R}$ and $\mathrm d$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]), is surjective with kernel the image of $\delta$. Hence $$I/I^2\xrightarrow{\ \delta\ }\bigoplus_{s\in S}S\,\mathrm d[s]\xrightarrow{\ \pi\ }\Omega_{S/R}\to0$$ is exact, i.e. $H_0(\mathrm{NL}_{S/R})=\operatorname{coker}\delta\cong\Omega_{S/R}$.
